subject: Civil Engineering
title: Desalination: Drinking the Ocean
description: A quick, practical guide to Desalination: Drinking the Ocean.

hook.text: 97.5% of Earth's water is salty. If we could drink it, water scarcity would vanish.

buildup.text: Reverse osmosis forces seawater through membranes — salt stays behind, fresh water passes.

discovery.text: Energy recovery devices recapture pressure from the brine — cutting energy use by 60%.

twist.text: Brine discharge harms marine life — concentrated salt dumped back into the ocean.

climax.text: Israel gets 80% of its drinking water from desalination — the world leader.

punchline.text: The ocean is infinite water, but making it drinkable costs energy.

quiz.question: What environmental concern is associated with desalination?
options: It removes too much salt from the ocean, affecting currents
Concentrated brine discharge harms marine ecosystems near outfall points
The membranes release microplastics into the drinking water

details.summary: Desalination removes dissolved salts from seawater or brackish water to produce fresh drinking water. Reverse osmosis, the dominant modern method, forces water through semi-permeable membranes at high pressure, rejecting 99.5% of dissolved salts.
details.whyItMatters: Desalination provides drought-proof water supply independent of rainfall. As freshwater scarcity intensifies globally, desalination is increasingly essential for water security in arid coastal regions.
takeaways: Reverse osmosis membranes reject 99.5% of dissolved salts from seawater
Energy recovery devices capture pressure from concentrate reject to reduce total energy by 60%
Modern desalination produces water at $0.50-1.50 per cubic meter depending on scale

faq.question: How does reverse osmosis desalination work?
faq.answer: Seawater is pressurized to 55-70 bar and forced through semi-permeable membranes that allow water molecules to pass while blocking dissolved salts. About 40-50% of the feed water passes through as fresh product water. The remaining concentrated brine is discharged.

faq.question: What are the main environmental concerns about desalination?
faq.answer: Concentrated brine discharge can harm marine organisms near the outfall if not properly dispersed. Energy consumption contributes to carbon emissions unless powered by renewables. Intake structures can entrap marine life.
